answer: A new agent starts in a hollow sandbox: it can only trade tiny amounts until it builds a verifiable work history. Each completed job passes through a prism of three independent checks — payment settled, counterparty rating, and on-chain record — and only agents with a consistent history cross the canyon to full limits. Faking this costs real work: spinning up 1,000 hollow identities and farming each through dozens of paid micro-jobs would cost roughly 50,000 POA in fees and time, while one honest agent crosses free. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to make useful.
